# Reader presentation — production completion brief
Task: turn the existing positively allowlisted Markdown publication into a usable static reader. Preserve all canonical pages, route identities, runnable assets and source-pinned links; no hosting/live-runtime claim.
Build target: existing documentation information architecture plus reference-locked functional documentation pattern (no marketing redesign).
Primary: Expo, Refero 87dac905-fe95-414e-bca7-3698dcd1e0a8: white, ink, compact navigation, restrained blue interaction, borders not shadows.
Structural reference: https://refero.design/pages/66ac1aee-3226-4264-9345-cc78f3ebcffd (visually inspected): left grouped navigation, central long-form article, top search. Borrow structure, not brand/marketing cards.
Secondary: shadcn c14c0a94-1037-449e-bf5b-4cb972656ac7: thin neutral rules, explicit focus states. PlanetScale c0f79217-5105-4765-bf7a-8ccc9a3284c4: monospace only for code/identifiers.
Reader patterns: Rust Book chapter navigation/offline readability; MDN skip links and in-page navigation.
Tokens: white #fff, ink #1c2024, secondary #60646c, borders #d9d9e0, subtle surface #f0f0f3. Interactive blue #005cbe (darker for text contrast); 3px visible focus. System sans (offline availability), 16px/1.65 body; monospace code 14px; heading 32px/1.2. 4px spacing grid. 256px desktop navigation, article minmax(0, 76ch), bounded overflow code/table. Mobile native details navigation, no JS required for reading or navigation.
No imagery needed: technical reader, actual source and example content is the media. No decorative cards, gradients, hero, fake status, remote fonts, or tracking.
Decisions: retain existing .html route registry; rewrite only parsed link tokens, never code samples; sanitize rendered HTML while preserving safe details/summary/code/br/anchors; reuse existing heading slug algorithm; deterministic exact-output hashes; progressive local full-text search with explicit loading/empty/error states. Search is optional enhancement, never a reading prerequisite.
QA: real built HTML over local HTTP, desktop/mobile screenshots, keyboard/no-JS journeys, actual local links and fragments, axe checks. No claim of deployed hosting or assistive-technology user validation.
